turns.reason: First reconnaissance: get a near top-down view of the whole course to read the directions of the straight wire segments, the start pose and the exit sleeves relative to the floor rulers.

Top view: course heads ~25-27 deg from +X (NE-ish). Visible twist 1 lies between the start and the tunnel entrance (gray A goes to the left/north side mid-twist). Hidden part goes steeply SE inside the tunnel, exit straight again at ~25 deg. Now zoom on the white board to read the hidden stretch (bends, twist 2).

Turn-3 side view: wire heights are constant (level course). Twist 1 (visible) has its mid-crossing ~6.9 studs ahead of the pivot (X~14.1) and spans ~X 11.2-17.2. Tunnel west face X~19.7. The pan did not land where expected: the image centre was underground near Y~-10, which suggests pan Y and Z may be applied with negated sign. Moving 2.8 studs along +x stays safely before the twist. I will test the pan by aiming at the board (27,47,5.7) with pan=[6,-27,-5.7] to read the hidden stretch.

The board shows the hidden stretch. In the top view, the wire enters near the NW of the tunnel and makes a right bend of about 91 deg (heading 28 to -63). After a straight of about 4, a lens of about 6.8 studs marks twist 2, then the wire runs straight SSE to near the SE corner. Bend 2 is probably just outside the tunnel. In the south view the upper line dips in a cup down to the lower line, so in twist 2 A rises through the course-left side: roll +180 about payload x. I am now at s=3.6, at the start of twist 1. A small safe step: move 0.8 and roll -10, then a high top view of the whole course to measure the twist-1 lens, the tunnel box and bend 2.

This top view confirms the plan: gray wire A bulges to course-left (NNW) in twist 1, so the -x roll sign is right. The tunnel top spans about X 19.7-30.8 and Y 16.7-31.2, and the wires enter the W face near (19.6,29.6). The twist-1 profile (linear or smooth) is uncertain, so the angle at s=4.2 could be 7-34 deg. Small safe step: roll another -10 (total -20) and move 0.6 to s=4.2, then a top view centred on twist 1 to measure the wire lateral offsets and the ring alignment.

Pivot is at s=4.2 with roll -20, no contact so far. The twist-1 lens in the top view runs from about s=2.8 to 10.3, mid about 6.6-6.9. Two shapes fit: linear (s0~2.6, about 21-23 deg/stud, wire angle about 33 deg here) or smooth cosine (about 18 deg here). I roll -8 more (total -28), which stays within about 10 deg of both. Then a top view with az=28 puts the course left-to-right and course-left up, so the wire separation just behind and ahead of the payload shows which shape is right. Separation at s~3.5: linear about 1 stud, smooth about 0.35.

Course-aligned top view: the twist-1 lens starts at about s=2.3 and closes at about s=10.0, with its middle near 6.2-6.5. There was no jam at s=3.6 with roll 0, so the twist eases in smoothly or starts a little late. Rolls are set for the middle of each next step, keeping the mismatch under about 20° for every model that fits: roll to -46 and move 0.8 (to s=5.0), then roll to -66 and move 0.8 (to s=5.8). Then a south side view (az=0, whose pan rule is known) centred on the payload. It should show the ring-A vs wire height match and where the wires cross at mid-twist.

The south view shows the wires crossing about 0 to 0.2 studs ahead of the pivot, so the middle of twist 1 is at s=6.0 to 6.1. No jam at s=3.6 with roll 0 or at s=4.2 with roll 20, so the twist eases in smoothly (a constant-rate twist would have jammed). Each roll is set to the wire angle at the middle of the next 0.6 step: 90, then 112.5, then 128. This keeps the expected mismatch about 11 deg (limit about 20). The camera stays on the south view to check ring heights against wire heights afterwards.

South view at s=7.04, roll -128: both rings sit on their wires (B upper-right on brown, A lower-left on gray), so no jam. A smooth twist with its middle near s=6.0 fits all passes so far, and I have already passed mismatches of 15 deg or more. Next steps keep the mismatch within about 14 deg for a middle anywhere in 5.9-6.1: roll to 138.5 and move 0.8 (to s=7.83), then roll to 162 and move 1.0 (to s=8.84). Then I re-read the board at the closest zoom to get bend 1, twist 2 and the exit before entering the tunnel. If a move is blocked, the camera step is skipped and I will see the payload.

This view shows the board clearly. Top-view panel: right bend just inside the W face, then a straight at about -60 to -63 deg, then a lens (twist 2) from about (25.6,25.3) to (29.4,19.0), drawn end about (30.0,17.8). The wire probably leaves through the S face near the SE corner, so bend 2 is outside and visible. Side panel: the upper line dips in a U cup down to the lower line, with the crossing near the bottom. As in twist 1's south view, that means the top wire lags in X. At heading -60 that is course-right, so twist 2 = +180 about payload x. Now I finish twist 1 (roll to -180) and slide straight to s=11.43, still outside the tunnel (W face at s=12.4). Then a high top view covering the payload, the tunnel and the SE exit, to measure where the middle straight leaves the tunnel, its heading, bend 2 and the sleeves. With those I can place bend 1's vertex precisely.

Bend 1 starts about here (the pivot is about 0.9 west of the W face). Several fits put the vertex about 3.7-4.3 studs ahead with radius about 3.5-4.6. A first chord (yaw +11.5 to the right, since z is down, then move 1.5) stays within 0.2 of the wire for every case that fits, so it is safe. Then a centred top view of bend 2 to fit its arc and the middle straight, which pins down the rest of bend 1.

Fitting the exit view, the bend-1 arc radius is about 4.07 (same as bend 2) and its vertex is about 4.13 ahead of P0 on the entry line. This is consistent with the tunnel being the drawn stretch's bounding box plus a 1.0 margin, and with the middle line passing through (29.8, 17.7). The pivot is at entry-frame (a 1.470, r 0.317), on the arc at about 20 deg, turned 11.5. Next: chord to the arc at 45 deg (yaw +19.5, move 1.71), then chord to 67.5 deg (yaw +25.5, move 1.59). Then a board view to time twist 2.

Bend 1 is going cleanly: the dead-reckoned pivot sits on the R 4.07 arc at about 67 deg, turned 56.5. I finish it with yaw +22.5, a 1.59 chord to T2 (24.35,28.00) and yaw +11, giving middle heading -62.4. The board side view shows a U whose bottom touches the lower line. That means the top wire (B) goes via course-right, so twist 2 is +180 about payload x, and the U-bottom crossing sits at the twist centre's X. Readings of the centre disagree: the side view gives X about 27.0, so d 5.6-6.0, while my top-view lens readings give d 6.6-7.2. I need better resolution before the twist. I am taking a level close-up of the board with the camera north of the tunnel, about 2-3x closer.

Close-up of the board's side panel: the frame spans x 252.5-814, which maps to tunnel X 19.7-30.8. The drawn upper line starts at x≈300 (X≈20.7, the top of the bend-1 arc, which matches my bend model and the tunnel box). The U's left and right sides average to x≈626.5, so the twist-2 centre is at X≈27.11. From T2 (24.35, 28.00) at heading -62.4, that puts the centre at c≈5.95 along the straight. The top wire (B) drops on the U's LEFT side, lagging in X, so it passes on course-right. That confirms twist 2 = +180 about payload x. Older low-resolution top-view reads put the centre at 6.4-6.8, a conflict worth about 18 deg of roll. I need a sharp top view of the lens (it gives both X and Y, so it does not depend on lateral offset) and the middle-straight heading. First a safe move of 2.6 along the middle straight to d≈2.59. Every likely model gives at most about 8-11 deg of twist there; c=5.95 gives about 1 deg. Then a level, slightly upward board view from north of the tunnel at about 39 px per real stud, showing the lens and the side-view U together.

This board view shows twist 2 clearly. The side panel's U-crossing gives the twist centre at X about 27.13. The top-panel lens runs from about (25.59, 25.93) to (28.64, 19.99), with its centre near (27.13, 22.9). That puts the twist centre about 3.2 ahead of the pivot (d_c about 5.78), with the true line about 0.12 left of my track. The camera tilt (el -4) makes the vertical scale uncertain, and the side panel's wire spacing (96 px, about 2.7 studs, not 2.95) hints the board may be vertically compressed. If so, the centre could be up to about 0.4-0.7 later. Roll +10 then move 0.96 keeps the mismatch at or below about 12 deg for every model that fits, and stays close to the line. Then a level (el 0) board view gives an undistorted read of the lens and the wire spacing to fix the twist schedule.

The 0.96 move from d=2.59 at roll +10 was stopped by wire B, at an unknown point inside the tunnel. The board's south panel shows a U-shaped dip with the crossing below centre. That means the top wire (B) shifts west, which is course-right, so twist 2 should be + about payload x. The likely cause: the twist started earlier or runs faster than I modelled, so the wire is now about 26 deg while I am at 10 (estimated tolerance about 16 deg). A + rotation tests this. If the twist really runs the other way, the rotation is stopped immediately and my roll stays about 10. If it passes, I am roughly aligned and take two twist steps from the model (sine profile, L=8.4). Each roll leads the wire by about 5 deg and each move lets it get about 11 deg ahead. A stopped move then tells me the wire angle is my roll plus about 16. The camera goes first, as a top view over my position, to check whether anything shows through the tunnel.

Last batch passed: roll 31 and 47.5 with no jam, so twist 2 is positive. Wire angle now is estimated 54-58 (the previous block anchors it at roughly 26 when I stopped). Board lens centre is at d about 5.6. Four smooth-twist models fit everything so far (twist length 7.7 to 9.5). For each step I roll to the predicted wire angle at the middle of the next 0.447 move: roll 63, move, roll 77, move, roll 91.5. Predicted mismatch stays within about ±10.6 deg for every model. The camera stays on the top view.

Twist 2 continues cleanly: rolls of 63, 77 and 91.5 all passed. I keep the 0.447 step pattern and set each roll near the angle that minimises the worst mismatch over the four twist models (worst case about 11-12 deg). This turn: move 0.447 at roll 91.5, roll to 105.5, move 0.447, roll to 119.5, move 0.447. The view stays on top since the payload is hidden in the tunnel.

Last batch passed: twist-2 roll is 119.5 at D=2.235 (D = studs past P*). Several twist models still fit the one block and all passes: short twists with a low threshold (about 12 deg) and long twists with a higher one (about 17.5). I set each roll to keep every model inside its threshold; the more likely ones keep at least about 3 deg spare. This turn: roll +13 to 132.5, move 0.447, roll +12 to 144.5, move 0.447, roll +11 to 155.5. Next turn: move 0.515, roll to 167, move 0.85, roll to 180, then move to the bend-2 start.

Twist 2 is going cleanly. This batch finishes it: move 0.515 at roll 155.5, roll to 167, move 0.85, roll to 180. Every model in my table stays within its jam threshold, with the most extreme ones at under 1 deg spare. The final move of 2.44 is straight along the middle line to about 0.27 past the bend-2 start T3 (29.56,18.04), at about (29.67,17.79), the first corner of my bend path. Bend 2 is a left turn, so +yaw about z now that z is up. I'll follow it as straight cuts that alternate slightly outside and inside the arc (about 0.07 each way), using diagonal moves so only 2 yaws are needed (5 actions instead of 7). I check with a top view once the pivot leaves the tunnel at the SE corner after the first cut.

The pivot was located from the three arrow tips in the top view: x tip at image (597,553), y tip at (621,479), z tip at (580,517). Pivot height is taken as 5.675, arrow length comes out at 2.30. This puts the pivot at about (30.08, 17.00), on my middle line (lateral -0.02). It is 0.9 further along than dead reckoning, so it sits about 16 deg into bend 2 and about 0.18 outside the arc. That fits no jam at the current 16 deg tilt. A fit of the visible arc plus the exit line gives R about 3.95 (range 3.5-4.4), centre about (33.08, 19.83). I check each step against 7 model variants. Plan: two cuts of about 31 deg, with yaw set to the average of the wire's direction at each end. Rotate +31.5 to heading -30.9, then move dx 2.144 dy 0.118 (world (1.90,-1.00)) to Q1 (31.98,16.00). Rotate +31 to heading 0.1, then move dx 2.15 to Q2 (34.13,16.00). Rotate +27.5 to exit heading 27.6. Worst-case deviation is 0.37 at tilt 14 deg or below, with at least 0.14 to spare in every model. Next turn: measure Q2, then a single move about 10.3 along the exit to the sleeve centre.

All bend-2 moves and turns passed, and the payload is out of the tunnel at heading 27.6 with roll 0 (z up, ring A on the gray upper wire). In the top view the arrow tips give the pivot at about (34.32,15.91), near my dead-reckoned (34.13,16.00). The green sleeves run from about (41.92,20.14) to (44.47,21.42), so their centre is about (43.20,20.78). That is about 10.13-10.28 ahead along the exit heading and 0.03-0.20 to the left. One straight move of dx 10.15, dy +0.10 (world 8.95, 4.80) brings the pivot to about (43.27,20.71) or (43.08,20.80), in the middle of the sleeves. A camera view of the sleeves follows in case the goal does not trigger.
